name: libxsmm-full512-row-half-first-traversal
hypothesis: Change traversal within each packed 64-row band: compute the first 32 output rows across all sixteen column panels, then compute the second 32 rows across all sixteen panels. Keeping one packed row half active across a complete column sweep may improve reuse; this is unverified. At 16 FP32 lanes, four ZA.S tiles form one 32x32 output block. Both K loops, FMOPA order, stores, 256-byte scratch stride, 128 KiB allocation and SME transitions remain unchanged. After each sweep, reset B by 2048 bytes and advance C by 63488 bytes from its post-sweep position. The second half uses scratch base+128. These offsets cover each output block once and preserve the next 64-row band's starting pointers. General sizes, tails, n<=0, the unused helper and both complete license notices remain unchanged. This traversal is absent from the supplied measured history. No tools or tests were run. Compilation, full-GEMM correctness and performance remain untested; throughput above 1800 GFLOP/s is not established. Use the unchanged base source for fresh paired controls under the fixed gates and unchanged power settings.
